claims.claim: The report says most Gateway DNS queries were unaffected, while queries with identity-based DoH rules failed.
Every Gateway DNS query failed during the June 12 outage.
Exactly 10,000 Gateway users were affected by the June 12 outage.
A third-party storage failure disrupted Workers KV and services that depended on it.
The report establishes why the portion of CDN traffic that failed to reroute was not rerouted.
A single named customer generated all the extra Zero Trust registration traffic during the outage.
Services began recovering at 20:23 UTC, before service-level objectives returned to their pre-incident level at 20:28 UTC.
All planned Workers KV redundancy improvements were complete when services recovered from the outage.
The report gives an exact calendar date for completing all planned Workers KV storage redundancy work.
The report says DNS over HTTPS using cloudflare-dns.com remained available while queries to the withdrawn resolver IP addresses were disrupted.
Every DNS transport and resolver address was completely unavailable worldwide during the July 14 incident.
Exactly one million individual users experienced the July 14 resolver outage.
The June 6 configuration error remained dormant until the July 14 change refreshed the associated routes.
The report identifies the BGP hijack as the cause of the resolver outage.
One engineer authored both the June 6 and July 14 configuration changes.
Readvertising the prefixes at 22:20 UTC restored roughly 77% of prior traffic, with normal traffic levels observed at 22:54 UTC.
All required edge-server IP bindings were already restored immediately after the 22:20 UTC revert.
The report states the exact date when deprecation of the legacy addressing systems will be complete.
The report says existing Access sessions were unaffected even while authentication failed for most users.
All customers on the old FL proxy engine received HTTP 5xx errors because of the bad feature file.
Exactly 250,000 customers received HTTP 5xx errors during the November 18 outage.
A database permissions change introduced duplicate metadata rows that made the Bot Management feature file too large.
The report confirms that a cyberattack caused the November 18 network outage.
The same engineer approved both the database permissions change and the Bot Management runtime feature limit.
Core traffic was largely normal by 14:30 UTC, and all systems were functioning normally by 17:06 UTC.
All systems were fully back to normal at 14:30 UTC.
The report supplies an exact completion date for each listed follow-up hardening project.

references.rationale: The service table explicitly distinguishes most DNS queries from identity-based DoH exceptions.
Most Gateway DNS queries were unaffected; the universal failure claim conflicts with the stated exceptions.
The report describes Gateway impact but gives no affected-user count establishing or excluding this number.
The storage dependency failure and its cascading impact are explicitly described.
The report explicitly says that portion of traffic is under investigation. That conflicts with asserted established explanation under the literal reporting contract.
Additional registration traffic is described, but the source neither identifies a single generating customer nor excludes that attribution.
The timeline states recovery beginning at 20:23 and service-level objectives returning at 20:28.
After recovery, redundancy and related workstreams remained actively in flight, conflicting with completion of all planned improvements.
The report says work is being accelerated and remains in flight, but supplies no exact calendar completion date. Omission alone is not explicit contradiction.
DoH through the domain uses different addresses and remained available; withdrawn addresses were unreachable.
DoH through cloudflare-dns.com and some UDP traffic remained mostly unaffected, contradicting universal unavailability.
Global impact and a majority of users are described, without an exact individual-user count establishing or excluding one million.
The earlier error had no immediate impact; a later change triggered the global routing refresh.
The source explicitly says the hijack was unrelated and not the outage cause.
Changes and peer review are described, but no shared author is established or explicitly excluded.
The restoration section reports partial recovery to about 77%, then normal traffic at 22:54.
About 23% of the fleet had lost required bindings and still needed reconfiguration after readvertisement.
Deprecation and accelerated migration are planned or active, without an exact completion date. This is missing reporting, not an explicitly conflicting date.
The Access table explicitly separates existing sessions from widespread authentication failures.
The report says old-engine customers did not see errors; they instead received incorrect bot scores, with impact depending on rules.
The report describes error traffic and affected systems without an exact affected-customer count establishing or excluding this number.
The permissions change exposed additional schema metadata; duplicate features exceeded the runtime limit.
An attack was an initial mistaken suspicion; the source explicitly excludes malicious activity as the cause.
The change and runtime limit are documented, but no approving engineer or common approval identity is established or excluded.
The source distinguishes main-traffic recovery from the later restoration of all systems.
Further service restarts and mitigation continued until 17:06, conflicting with complete recovery at 14:30.
Follow-up work is listed as begun, with no exact per-project calendar completion dates. Missing discussion alone does not establish contradiction.

source_cautions.cf-kv12-2025: The service table reports 90.22% failed KV requests while a later figure caption rounds to 91%. Claims avoid treating these as conflicting exact rates. The CDN rerouting exception remains under investigation.
source_cautions.cf-dns14-2025: Routing refresh at 21:48 precedes traffic decline at 21:52; impact end at 22:54 precedes incident resolution at 22:55. Claims preserve stages and transport/address exceptions.
source_cautions.cf-nov18-2025: Intro and chart use 11:20 onset while the timeline labels impact start at 11:28; bypass prose uses 13:04/13:10 and timeline 13:05. Claims avoid a single exact onset/bypass time and preserve all full text. The report includes hypotheses, unaffected sessions and proxy-dependent impact.

preparation: Same-assistant controlled claims after source inspection, before new model outcomes; complete extracted report retained.
